reasons: The legacy path has no test visible in this packet.
Many fixed limits (driver counts, appendix size, label lengths) are set by hand.
The chart takes a limited number of projects without saying so.
The file has several long functions that are hard to follow without the rest of the deck code.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: File purpose and imports
sections.what: Explains that the file builds the recipe deck in a fixed order: cover, summary, agenda, pillars, one page per pillar, assessment, then appendix. It brings in the result types, citation helper and the newer content builder.
sections.why: Lets the deck follow the reference layout while the content stays specific to each run.
sections.watch_out: Pillar names must come from the data, as the header says. Hard-coding a name here would break that rule.

sections.name: RecipeDeckParts
sections.title: Shape of the deck inputs
sections.what: Defines the set of run results this builder reads, including the assessments list.
sections.why: Narrows the input to only the parts the deck needs.
sections.watch_out: If a new field is read here, it must also exist on the result type or the types will disagree.

sections.name: factById
sections.title: Finding a fact by its ID
sections.what: Returns the fact with the matching ID, or nothing if none matches.
sections.why: Used to show a quote beside each sub-driver.

sections.name: truncateAtWord
sections.title: Shortening text at a word boundary
sections.what: Cuts text to a maximum length at the last space, removes trailing punctuation, and adds an ellipsis. The cover summary limit is 300 characters.
sections.why: Stops words from being split across lines on the slide. The comment records that an older 120-character cut split words.
sections.watch_out: If the text has no space before the limit, the cut lands in the middle of a word.

sections.name: buildReferenceRecipeSlides
sections.title: Choosing old or new layout
sections.what: Uses the legacy builder when the methodology has no source register, and otherwise uses the newer content builder.
sections.why: Keeps saved older results rendering the way they did before.
sections.watch_out: The choice depends only on whether the source register is present, so an unexpected missing field silently switches the layout.

sections.name: buildLegacyReferenceRecipeSlides (part 1)
sections.title: Cover and executive summary slides
sections.what: Builds the cover with the industries and a summary, then the executive summary with coverage, portfolio mix, counts and the top recommendation, plus an outcome chart.
sections.why: The coverage line says how many scope projects were actually analysed.
sections.watch_out: The cover summary is cut to 300 characters without a clear sign to the reader.

sections.name: buildLegacyReferenceRecipeSlides (part 2)
sections.title: Agenda and pillar overview
sections.what: Builds the agenda listing each pillar, then an overview slide with a chart of facts per pillar, and a pillar overview line for each pillar.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a reader see which themes had evidence before reading each one.
sections.watch_out: Chart labels are cut to 18 characters after the first comma, so two pillars can end up with the same label.

sections.name: buildLegacyReferenceRecipeSlides (part 3)
sections.title: Splitting each pillar into pages
sections.what: For each pillar, writes each sub-driver's text, why it matters, its strength and risk counts and up to three quotes. It adds a closing block showing facts not attached to any driver, and the sum check. Each driver block is kept together as one page unit.
sections.why: The comments say the counts must add up: sub-driver facts plus unattached facts equal the pillar total.
sections.watch_out: Page units are recorded by line position, so the bullets and their unit list must stay in step or page breaks will land in the wrong place.

sections.name: buildLegacyReferenceRecipeSlides (part 4)
sections.title: Pillar slides and assessment slide
sections.what: Creates one slide per pillar with its bullets and page units, then an assessment slide listing patterns, recommendations and a cost overrun chart.
sections.why: The assessment slide gathers the findings in one place for the reader.
sections.watch_out: The overrun chart takes only the first eight projects in list order, and the footnote does not say that others were left out.

sections.name: buildLegacyReferenceRecipeSlides: for
sections.title: Appendix pages and final order
sections.what: Ranks relevant facts so pillar-linked, verified, sourced facts come first, caps the appendix at 48 facts in pages of eight, then returns all slides in order with citations added.
sections.why: The cap keeps the file usable, and the ranking puts the most supported facts first.
sections.watch_out: The appendix footnote explains the cut only when facts were actually dropped, and the cap of 48 is a fixed number.

summary: Chooses the slide layout for a recipe deck and builds the older layout used for saved results, with pillar pages, a fact appendix and citations.
purpose: Turns a run's results into the ordered list of slides for the deck, following the reference megaprojects layout.
why: The header says the slide order follows a reference design, while pillar names come from the data so each run stays specific.
how: The main function checks whether the methodology has a source register. If it does, it uses the newer content builder. If not, it uses the legacy builder, which writes the cover, executive summary, agenda, pillar overview, one page group per pillar, an assessment slide and a capped fact appendix, then adds citations in order.
inputs: The run result parts: pillars, facts, patterns, recommendations, projects, totals, methodology and scope, plus optional subtitle, coverage and mode note.
outputs: An ordered list of slide blocks, each with a title, bullets, footnotes, optional chart and metadata.
risks: Older results without a source register silently get the legacy layout. The appendix is capped at 48 facts, and the legacy text is shortened, so some information is not shown in the deck.
debug: If the slide order looks wrong, check whether the methodology has a source register, since that decides which builder runs. If the pillar totals do not add up, compare the driver counts with the not-attached count. If a slide is cut short, check the length limits.
